source.title: Survey of State Criminal History Information Systems, 2022
source.authors: Becki R. Goggins and Dennis A. DeBacco, SEARCH (BJS-funded grant report, award 15BJS-23-GK-00052-NCHI)
notes: No CSV/XLS data-tables zip is offered on the BJS page; only the full-report PDF (65 pp). All figures read from the PDF tables.

Data are a snapshot as of December 31, 2022; survey fielded May-July 2023. All 50 states, DC and Guam responded; American Samoa, New Mexico, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands did not report (nr).

Subjects: Table 2 'Number of subjects (individual offenders) in state criminal history file, 2020 and 2022', column '2022 total' (manual + automated files). Numbers rounded to nearest 100. Counts only the criminal history file, not the master name index.

Sealed/expunged: Table 5a 'Record sealing and expungements, 2022 (continued)'. These are counts of RECORDS sealed/expunged by the repository in 2022, not subjects; no subject-level sealing/expungement counts exist in the report. Null where cell is blank, 'na' (not available), 'nr' (not reported), '-' (undefined in legend), state does not track, or state does not seal (footnote a).

Table 5 note: record sealing and expungement definitions and practices vary widely across the states. Sealed = restricted from public access, generally unavailable for employment/licensing but accessible on a limited basis; Expunged = all hard copy and electronic information destroyed.

Caveat (Note to readers): use caution in drawing comparisons between the results of earlier surveys and the data reported here; trend comparisons may not accurately reflect the status of each state's records.

Table 5a anomalies as printed: Alabama shows 844 expunged with a blank 'tracks expunged' cell; DC shows 'No' for tracking expungements but 615 in the count column. Cross-check: the 50 state+DC values extracted sum exactly to the Table 5a Total row (1,190,236 sealed; 414,056 expunged).

Report narrative (p.6): 'Twenty-six states, the District of Columbia, and Guam track the number of records that are sealed. In 2022, nearly 1.2 million records were sealed.' 'Thirty-four states and Guam track the number of records that are expunged. In 2022, over 414,000 records were expunged.'
